target_customer: SaaS and professional services providers, later law firms, that want upfront payment while offering buyers flexible terms
problem: Providers wait for large invoices to be paid while business buyers want to spread payments over months.
business_model: Fees on B2B buy now pay later and invoice payments, funded by credit facilities
product_category: B2B buy now pay later and invoice payments

founders.name: Philip Kelvin
founders.background_notes: Former CFO of proptech startup Trussle.

founders.name: Beau Allison
founders.background_notes: Former head of engineering at Trussle.

technical_complexity.rationale: Credit decisioning, payment rails and lender integrations are standard fintech engineering with regulatory overhead.

defensibility.rationale: Access to debt funding and credit data helped, but the model was replicable by other B2B BNPL providers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Legal software vendor Elite acquired it on January 6, 2025 to add payments to its law firm suite.

market_need_then: Providers wanted upfront cash on large invoices; the 2022 press coverage describes BNPL moving into B2B, but no dated spend figures were retrieved.

branding.name_origin: Evokes the financial term tranche, a portion of a payment (inferred; no source states it).
branding.domain_note: Owns tranch.com (exact match); acquisition date unknown.

identity.logo: A block payment cut into four tranches and rearranged into a T, nicknamed the butter knife by the design studio.
identity.visual_style: Identity by Lovework Studio inspired by slicing videos, in June 2022.
identity.voice_and_tone: Payment ease, turning large payments into bite sized chunks.

branding.brand_signature: The sliced block T logo and chunked payments concept

rebrands.why: Identity coverage says the company was previously called UpCash; the reason is not given.

branding.community_and_virality: Design press coverage by It's Nice That in June 2022.

brand_strength.rationale: A well covered design identity with a concept matching the product, but a B2B niche brand with limited consumer awareness.

outcome_analysis: Tranch raised a 3.5 million pound pre-seed in May 2022, then a roughly 5 million seed with a 95 million credit facility in January 2023, while its payment volume with large law firms more than tripled in 2024. Elite acquired it in January 2025 to embed payments in law firm billing, a vertical fit exit with undisclosed terms.
notes: Pre-seed was 3.5 million pounds in equity and debt; no dollar amount was converted, so amount_usd is null. Press headlines say 100 million seed, combining about 5M equity and a 95M credit facility (BuiltIn), so the facility is recorded as debt. Company site returned 403. Competitors left empty because comparison pages found (Resolve, Hokodo, Billie) are dated 2026, not around founding.
